title: Trump sons' drone ventures and the Pentagon's Drone Dominance programme
summary: The deals and letters are documented: the brothers hold an indirect stake (via American Ventures) in the Powerus/Aureus Greenway merger (announced 2026-03-09, closed ~2026-10-01), which then won an up-to-$90M Air Force IDIQ and an $82M order; the WSJ reported in May 2026 that the Pentagon was negotiating debt-and-equity funding with Unusual Machines, which co-led a $10M investment in Draganfly in Sep 2026. EO 14307 and the FCC's Dec 2025 foreign-drone Covered List do benefit domestic makers, and the Garcia/Warren IG letters and the $70M+ PitchBook tally are real. But no Unusual Machines equity deal had been announced by Nov 2026, the $12.8M 'DoD contract' was a Strategic Logix subcontract, and no evidence shows family intervention; all parties deny it.

sub_claims.statement: Eric Trump and Don Jr. back the Powerus / Aureus Greenway drone merger.
sub_claims.finding: Golf-course company Aureus Greenway Holdings announced a reverse merger with Rock Hill, SC drone maker Powerus on 2026-03-09 (value undisclosed). The brothers hold their stake indirectly through American Ventures: about 3% of Aureus at announcement, with filings indicating a 9.9% beneficial stake in the combined company. Dominari Securities, roughly 6% owned by each brother, raised about $9M including from Unusual Machines. The merger closed around 2026-10-01 under the ticker PUSA, with CEO Andrew Fox. A Manufacturing Dive headline describing it as closed in March is wrong.

sub_claims.statement: Powerus has won federal drone business since the merger.
sub_claims.finding: Its subsidiary Tandem Defense won an Air Force IDIQ in Aug 2026 with a ceiling of up to $90M (a ceiling, not committed money). In Oct 2026 Powerus announced an $82M order under it, and it reported $130M in signed orders by Nov 2026. It qualified for Drone Dominance Phase II but was not among the Phase I production winners or the Gauntlet II winners. It also placed a $16.9M components order with Unusual Machines. Advisory board member Keith Kellogg said 'it never hurts to have their name on something.' Audit note: outlets differ on whether the IDIQ was awarded in July or August 2026. It runs to mid-2028. The $82M October order was the second order under an existing government IDIQ. Most outlets tie it to the $90M Tandem vehicle, and one says that link rests on procurement records.

sub_claims.statement: The Pentagon is negotiating an equity stake in Don Jr.-advised Unusual Machines under the $1.1B Drone Dominance programme.
sub_claims.finding: On 2026-05-28 the WSJ reported months of talks with UMAC, PDW and Neros on funding that could combine debt and equity. Coverage tied the talks to the roughly $1.1B Drone Dominance push, but the vehicle is OSC lending. UMAC rose about 57-65% on the report. PDW (a conditional commitment of up to $820M, 2026-07-31) and Neros (up to $450M, 2026-11-02) have since signed conditional OSC loans. No OSC release or filing naming UMAC was found as of mid-Nov 2026.

Reuters reported on 2026-09-28 that Unusual Machines and an unnamed US asset manager are buying 1,869,159 Draganfly shares at $5.35, about $10M in total, which is more than half of Draganfly's market cap of about $17.9M. The deal came weeks after Draganfly won a Canadian Armed Forces drone contract. The $5M-each split is unconfirmed.

sub_claims.statement: Trump executive orders on drones and restrictions on Chinese DJI benefit domestic makers.
sub_claims.finding: EO 14307 'Unleashing American Drone Dominance' (2025-06-06) prioritizes US-made drones in federal procurement but did not ban DJI. Effective 2025-12-22 the FCC put foreign-made UAS and critical components, including DJI, on its Covered List, citing the EO; this followed the FY25 NDAA-mandated review. Exemptions were later carved out for Blue UAS-listed and domestic products. NDAA-compliant suppliers like UMAC benefit structurally. Claims that Don Jr. personally pushed the DJI ban are unverified.

sub_claims.statement: Warren and Garcia wrote to the Pentagon Inspector General.
sub_claims.finding: Rep. Robert Garcia wrote to DoD IG Platte B. Moring III on 2026-05-08, citing Unusual Machines and the Powerus interceptor award. On 2026-08-04 Warren, Garcia, Blumenthal and Duckworth asked the IG to review about $3.2B in awards, plus $3.1B in options, to at least 15 companies tied to Trump-son-linked investors. Warren separately wrote to Hegseth about UMAC on 2026-05-06. No IG inquiry has been confirmed. Audit note: the $3.2B and $3.1B figures come from a Washington Post analysis, and they cover contracts, loans and investments, some at maximum potential value. An October 2026 ABC News analysis put the total above $6B. ABC then deleted the report, Donald Trump Jr. called it false, and the deletion was not explained, so that figure should not be relied on.

sub_claims.statement: Senate Democrats tallied $70M+ in federal contracts to 1789 Capital portfolio companies.
sub_claims.finding: On 2026-01-22/23 Warren, Blumenthal and Kim wrote to Hegseth. Citing PitchBook, they said 1789 portfolio companies received more than $70M in contracts between Apr and Nov 2025, including $45M to Cerebras in Apr 2025; the $620M Vulcan loan was cited separately. The figure has not been independently audited, and no lawbreaking is alleged. 1789 says it has 'absolutely zero involvement' in its companies' operations.

sub_claims.statement: The awards, financing talks or policy steps resulted from Trump family influence.
sub_claims.finding: No reporting or document shows a Trump son contacting officials about Powerus, UMAC, Draganfly or OSC. Don Jr.'s spokesperson says he never communicated with the administration on UMAC's behalf. Powerus says the brothers are passive investors.

corrections: Warren's letters call the Sept 2025 $12.8M award a DoD contract to Unusual Machines; the company describes it as an order from defense supplier Strategic Logix (RRSL line), i.e. a subcontract.
The Pentagon equity stake in Unusual Machines is reported as negotiated, not agreed; only peers PDW and Neros have closed OSC financing (as of mid-Nov 2026).
The Powerus/Aureus merger was announced in March 2026 and completed around Oct 1, 2026, not in March.
The DJI restrictions came via the FY25 NDAA review and the FCC Covered List (Dec 2025); EO 14307 itself did not ban DJI.
The Drone Dominance programme is a procurement effort; the equity-stake talks run through the Office of Strategic Capital.
PDW's OSC financing is a conditional loan commitment of up to $820M (31 Jul 2026), a figure missing from the original write-up (see C74).
denials_and_context: Powerus and the brothers' spokespeople say Eric and Don Jr. are passive investors with no operational role.
Don Jr.'s spokesperson says he never contacted the administration for Unusual Machines; UMAC CEO Allan Evans said he did nothing on the Army deal.
1789 Capital (Arthur Schwartz) denies any involvement in portfolio companies' operations; the senators allege no lawbreaking.
Demand for drones free of Chinese parts is bipartisan, NDAA-codified policy; most Drone Dominance Gauntlet winners (Skycutter, Neros, Perennial Autonomy) are not Trump-linked.
Award totals in the letters (e.g. $3.2B) mix contracts, loans and investments and include ceiling values, not money spent.
The original pages at warren.senate.gov, oversightdemocrats.house.gov and breakingdefense.com were not read directly; letter contents rely on press coverage.

An October 2026 ABC News tally of more than $6B in awards to Trump-son-backed firms was deleted by ABC. Donald Trump Jr. says it was false. A Pentagon official says investors and political ties play 'absolutely no role' in funding decisions.
